facts.text: Gloria Glens Park grew out of the 1880s Chippewa Lake Park, a vacation resort built by Oscar Townsend and the Cleveland, Lorain & Wheeling Railroad.
The village was created to house the many overnight guests who stayed at Chippewa Lake Park during weekend getaways.
Chippewa Lake Park closed its doors in 1978 after more than a century of operation, joining many other traditional amusement parks that vanished in the late 20th century.
Most of the bungalow‑style homes that line the streets today were originally built for park patrons and have since been updated for year‑round living.
Chippewa Lake Park preserves the memory of Ohio’s longest‑lived amusement park through vintage images and a captivating historical archive.
